body:
this is the current era as it sits on the site right now: showgirl, twelve songs in the track guide, four theories, four videos, and a timeline you can drag with your thumb.

the newest thing on it is dated august 11.

andrew lloyd webber — the cats and phantom composer, and one of the most serious private collectors of pre-raphaelite painting anywhere — posted a short video saying he had been listening to the album. "the track that really intrigues me is ‘the fate of ophelia.’"

he owns a version of the millais painting the whole era’s imagery keeps circling. it hangs, he said, in the room where they once had lunch. "so maybe she did."

he put no more weight on it than that maybe. neither will we.

longlivets.com/?era=tloas&utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=era-deep-cut

📷 taylor on the tonight show, october 2025 — todd owyoung/nbc via getty images. swipe for the era page itself.
why: SUBJECT SUBSTITUTED, and here is why. The calendar’s 08-15 23:00Z IG slot is an era-deep-cut on reputation with "vetted Vault photo with credit — era tile explicitly not acceptable here". (Historical note: at drafting time the library had no reputation-era photo and that PR was queue-only, so the slot was substituted to the TLOAS era page; superseded 2026-08-12 — the Taylor-photo PR added corpus photos, and this item now leads with a real TLOAS photo tile.) Rather than drop an Instagram day, the slot runs the strongest rung-1 asset the library does have — the real TLOAS era screenshot — with the same pillar and hook ("the artifact"). Everything in the caption is read off that screenshot (CURRENT ERA, 12-song track guide, 4 theories & eggs, 4 videos, the draggable timeline, the August 11, 2026 moment at the top of the feed) or traced to the Vault TLOAS item "Andrew Lloyd Webber hears his own Ophelia in ‘The Fate of Ophelia’" (2026-08-11, sourced Yahoo Creators + his own Instagram + WHYY): his Pre-Raphaelite collection, the "the track that really intrigues me" quote, and the carefully-hedged "maybe she did" about the Millais version in his house. The caption keeps his hedge intact instead of upgrading it to influence — the Vault says the Millais parallel was never confirmed by Taylor or her photographers, and this post says so. DEPLOY DEPENDENCY: needs #1903 deployed. | 2026-08-12 Taylor-photo standard (issue #2031, Joey directive): attached a real credited photograph of Taylor from the repo corpus (apps/web/lib/longlive/lenses.ts), rehosted under /social/library/photos/. Campaign renamed to a STORY-UNIQUE value: findPostedDuplicate treats same platform+campaign as an already-posted duplicate, so the old thematic bucket campaigns (heartbeat:*) would have false-skipped every post in a bucket after its first one landed. Upgraded to a carousel: Taylor photo as the grid tile, the product screenshot as slide 2. | 2026-08-15 third-party image policy (docs/decisions.md): the Getty-sourced photo tile (taylor-tloas-fallon-2025.jpg) was removed from the library and dropped from this item's media; it now runs on the TLOAS era screenshot alone, so mediaKind moved from "photo" to "site-screen" and the now-inapplicable mediaCredit/mediaSource were removed with it.
